clue.text: How the infection started at the beginning

definitions.meaning: a wound gets infected through a small cut in the skin, so the infection began from a little graze
starting with nothing done, right from the start of the job

explanation.definitionFit: An infection may begin from a little skin wound, and the idiom also means starting afresh from nothing.

clue.text: Were we out getting the morning paper

indicators.note: the word we is put out of the word were, leaving only its remaining pair

parts.note: AM is the usual abbreviation for morning, ante meridiem

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether they went out to buy the morning newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes WE from WERE, leaving RE; AM follows. 'getting' is a link, and 'the morning paper' wants to be one phrase, but 'paper' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A ream is a standard quantity of paper, about five hundred sheets.

clue.text: Domestic, we're told. Produced here

indicators.note: what we are told is heard rather than read, so a word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a domestic is a household servant, such as a maid

explanation.surface: A household note that something was made on the premises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Domestic' looks like an adjective but is a noun for a servant: a MAID, which sounds the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something produced in a given place was manufactured or created there.

clue.text: A number mad with desire

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for one hundred, a number
raving means wildly mad

explanation.surface: Someone driven wild by longing for something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A number' is the Roman numeral C; 'mad' looks like part of the definition phrase 'mad with desire', but it gives RAVING, and 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A craving is a strong longing or yearning for something.

clue.text: Nonchalant cockney description of a shaggy dog

indicators.note: London cockney speech drops the H at the start of words, so the leading letter goes

parts.note: a shaggy dog could be described as hairy, covered in long fur

explanation.surface: A Londoner describes a scruffy, long-haired dog in a casual way.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney speech, the accent of working-class east London, famously drops initial H, so HAIRY becomes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Airy can mean casual or lighthearted, unconcerned, as in an airy wave of the hand.

clue.text: Gathers their edible

definitions.meaning: a gather is a pucker or wrinkle in fabric, and cockle means to pucker
small edible shellfish sold at the seaside, so the second sense is shellfish one can eat

explanation.walkthrough: The clue as printed reads 'their'; it should be 'Gathers, they're edible', a double definition: puckers in cloth, and shellfish you can eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Cockles are puckers or wrinkles in material, and also small bivalve shellfish eaten in Britain.

clue.text: Pacifism as symbolised by the Venus de Milo!

definitions.meaning: laying down weapons, the policy of giving up an army's arms

definitions.text: as symbolised by the Venus de Milo!
definitions.meaning: the famous Greek statue has lost both its arms, so it is literally without arms

explanation.definitionFit: Giving up weapons is a peace policy, and the armless Venus de Milo is a statue literally deprived of its arms.

clue.text: Further education that's not very good

definitions.meaning: the class that comes after the first one, a next stage of schooling

explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the phrase is the next class up in school; as an idiom it means inferior or second-rate.

clue.text: Take pleasure in resembling

definitions.meaning: to enjoy something, be fond of it
similar to, in the manner of

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to enjoy, and the preposition means similar to.

clue.text: Kidology?

parts.note: the word for teasing or bluffing, read as the study of kids: the medical science of children

explanation.definitionFit: The branch of medicine dealing with children could jokingly be called the study of kids.

clue.text: If you will be a do-gooder, on your head be it!

definitions.text: If you will be a do-gooder, on your head be it!

parts.words: If you will be a do-gooder, on your head be it!
parts.note: the threatening idiom read literally: a saintly person wears a glowing ring above the head

explanation.definitionFit: Saints and the virtuous are pictured with a ring of light around the head.

clue.text: That's a lot of bunk!

parts.note: bunk usually means nonsense, but here it is a bed, and a very big one

explanation.definitionFit: An extra-large bed is plenty of place to sleep, a lot of bunk.

clue.text: It helps to keep down bills

definitions.text: It helps to keep down bills

parts.words: It helps to keep down bills
parts.note: not reducing expenses, but a heavy object holding loose papers such as invoices on a desk

explanation.definitionFit: A heavy desk ornament stops loose sheets, invoices included, from blowing away.

clue.text: Think Imyselfam harbouring a spirit

indicators.note: to harbour is to shelter within, so one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: the speaker referring to themself is me
gin is a spirit, a strong distilled drink

explanation.surface: A drinker suspects they have a ghost, or a drop of gin, inside them.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed text runs 'I myself am' together. 'am harbouring' puts A GIN inside ME, after I. 'spirit' suggests a ghost but is the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To imagine is to conceive or suppose, to think something up.

clue.text: Gets in the post

parts.note: not receiving letters by mail, but being paid while holding a job or position

explanation.definitionFit: Someone holding a job is paid a salary for it.

clue.text: Continued to think about retreating into the shade

indicators.note: one piece is put into the other, the shade surrounding it

parts.note: red is a shade, a colour

indicators.note: going backwards, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: to muse is to ponder or think about

explanation.surface: Someone went on pondering after withdrawing into the shadows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' turns MUSE to ESUM; 'into' puts that inside RED. 'shade' suggests shadow, but it means colour.
explanation.definitionFit: To resume is to carry on again after a break.

clue.text: Send one to, rather on the quiet!

indicators.note: the answer placed on, after, the letter for quiet makes the word for rather, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: would rather means prefer
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet

explanation.surface: A request to pass someone on, discreetly if possible.
explanation.walkthrough: Put P (piano, quiet) on the front of the answer and you get PREFER, 'rather'; so the answer is PREFER with P gone, signalled by 'on'.
explanation.definitionFit: To refer someone is to direct or pass them on to another person for help.

clue.text: Sport is almost all men talk about

indicators.note: the talk goes around the trimmed word, surrounding it

parts.note: gas is idle chatter, talk

indicators.note: the word men loses its final letter, so not quite all of it is used

explanation.surface: Sport is nearly all that men chat about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost all' cuts MEN to ME; 'about' puts GAS around it. 'talk about' reads as a phrase in the surface, but 'about' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Games are sports, organised competitive play.

clue.text: Delight in setting free a wild eagle

indicators.note: the letter a is released from the bird's name, removed from the pool
the remaining letters run wild, rearranged in any order

explanation.surface: Joy at releasing an untamed bird of prey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setting free' takes A out of EAGLE, leaving E, G, L, E; 'wild' scrambles those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Glee is joy, great merriment.

clue.text: He gets through-though only semi-literate

indicators.note: the name passes through the hyphenated word, its letters sitting inside it

explanation.surface: A man scrapes through, though he can barely read and write.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets through' signals the name runs inside 'semi-literate', across the hyphen; 'though only' is linking. 'He' is a man's name in crossword style.
explanation.definitionFit: Emil is a man's name, so it stands for a male person.

clue.text: Risk losing a day, to one's annoyance

indicators.note: the word for risk loses one letter, dropping it

parts.note: danger means risk or peril

explanation.surface: Missing a day's work would be a hazard and an irritation.
explanation.definitionFit: Anger is strong irritation or displeasure.

clue.text: A barrier to an insect that is immovable

parts.note: a dam is a barrier holding back water
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: An obstacle placed in an insect's path that will not budge.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamant means unyielding, refusing to change one's mind.

clue.text: Refuse? Nonsense!

definitions.meaning: an exclamation dismissing something as untrue

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both household waste and foolish talk.

clue.text: Is drawn back inside towards the centre

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other, enclosed by its letters
drawn back means the letters run backwards

explanation.surface: Something is pulled back into the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns DRAWN into NWARD; 'inside' puts that between the I and S of 'Is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Inwards means moving in the direction of the interior or middle.

clue.text: Decisions made during various reigns?

definitions.meaning: official judgements, such as a court's verdicts
the periods when monarchs held power, times of governing

explanation.definitionFit: Official judgements are pronouncements, and periods of governing could be playfully called the acts of reigning.

clue.text: Be on the turn or downright bad

indicators.note: turning round means the word is read backwards

parts.note: to be is to exist, to live

explanation.surface: Something going off, or simply rotten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the turn' sounds like food going sour, but it reverses LIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Evil means wicked, morally very wrong.

clue.text: Be a little thankful in the letter

parts.note: ta is a brief, informal British word for thanks

explanation.surface: Show some gratitude in what you write to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is everyday British slang for thank you. 'letter' suggests correspondence but means a Greek letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Beta is the second letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Firing this gun will come as a shock

definitions.text: Firing this gun will come as a shock

parts.words: Firing this gun will come as a shock
parts.note: an electric weapon that immobilises its target, and also a word for to shock or daze

explanation.definitionFit: The electroshock weapon is named for its effect, to daze or shock someone.

clue.text: Finished one day ahead

indicators.note: the day piece goes ahead of, in front of, the other piece

explanation.surface: A task completed with one day to spare.
explanation.definitionFit: Done means completed or over.

clue.text: Way in which a man utters a curse?

definitions.text: Way in which a man utters a curse?

parts.words: Way in which a man utters a curse?
parts.note: split into two words, a man's manner of speaking, his ..., is also a solemn curse

explanation.definitionFit: A malediction is a spoken curse, and split it describes a male way of speaking.

clue.text: It never allows you to have the last word

definitions.text: It never allows you to have the last word

parts.words: It never allows you to have the last word
parts.note: a reflected sound repeats whatever you shout, so it always speaks after you

explanation.definitionFit: A reflected sound repeats your words back, so it always speaks last.

clue.text: His complaint may be one of long standing

definitions.text: His complaint may be one of long standing

parts.words: His complaint may be one of long standing
parts.note: a long-running grievance, read literally as a commuter standing for ages on a crowded train holding a strap

explanation.definitionFit: A commuter who stands holding an overhead strap on a packed train grumbles about standing for long periods.
